<!-- README.md is generated from README.Rmd. Please edit that file -->

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.path = "man/figures/README-"
)
options(width = 100, pillar.width = 100)
# all montages of this README fit into 140 x 140 mm
tidymontage::tidymontage_options(width = 140, height = 140)

# Montages have a fixed physical size: save them at that size and embed the
# file, instead of drawing them into a device of arbitrary size.
montage_counts <- new.env()
knitr::opts_chunk$set(render = function(x, ...) {
  if (tidymontage::is_tidymontage(x)) {
    # number the montages of a chunk, so several don't overwrite each other
    label <- knitr::opts_current$get("label")
    n <- (montage_counts[[label]] %||% 0) + 1
    montage_counts[[label]] <- n
    name <- if (n == 1) label else paste0(label, "-", n)
    file <- file.path("man/figures", paste0("README-", name, ".png"))
    suppressMessages(tidymontage::save_montage(x, file, dpi = 200))
    knitr::knit_print(knitr::include_graphics(file, dpi = 200))
  } else {
    knitr::knit_print(x, ...)
  }
})
```

# tidymontage

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/jbengler/tidymontage/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jbengler/tidymontage/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of tidymontage is to streamline the creation of publication-ready
microscopy figure montages. It is a sibling of
[tidyplots](https://github.com/jbengler/tidyplots): a tidy data frame of images
goes in, montage components are added with pipeable verbs, and a figure of
exact physical size comes out, ready to be placed next to tidyplots with
[tidylayouts](https://github.com/jbengler/tidylayouts).

## Installation

You can install the development version of tidymontage from
[GitHub](https://github.com/jbengler/tidymontage) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("jbengler/tidymontage")
```

tidymontage is experimental: functions and arguments may still change.

## Getting started

The examples below use the microscope exports in `demo_images/`. They are not
part of the package (too large), so run them from a local checkout that has
the folder.

### Microscope files

tidymontage reads TIFF and OME-TIFF. Convert files in microscope formats
(CZI, ND2, LIF, OIR, VSI, ...) to OME-TIFF first, with ZEN, Fiji or the
Bio-Formats command line tool `bfconvert`; the article
[Getting your images in](https://jbengler.github.io/tidymontage/articles/getting-images-in.html)
shows how, including a script for whole folders.

### A first montage

Read the images, describe the experiment with dplyr, and hand them to
`tidymontage()`. Here two cells, one per mutant, become one column each, with
their channels as rows. Display ranges are **linked per channel**, so the
brightness of both mutants can be compared:

```{r first}
library(tidymontage)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

cells <- read_images(list.files("demo_images", "\\.ome\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE)) |>
  mutate(mutant = if_else(grepl("I56A", filepath), "I56A", "L59A"))

cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant)
```

The rest of this README first looks at the data model, the tibble of images,
and then at what `tidymontage()` can do with it.

## The data model

### One row per image

`read_images()` takes files or directories and returns a long tibble with one
row per image: per file, channel, z-slice and time point. The `img` column
holds lazy references to **greyscale** images; no pixels are read at this
point. Colours are only applied when a montage is drawn.

```{r read}
images <- read_images("demo_images")
images
```

How many images does each file contribute, and where did the metadata come
from?

```{r count}
images |>
  count(file = basename(filepath), meta_source, pixel_size_source, name = "images")
```

Channel labels, colours and calibration come straight from the microscope
metadata:

```{r channels}
images |>
  filter(grepl("Airyscan", filepath), z == 1) |>
  select(channel, channel_name, color, size_x, size_z, pixel_size, z_step)
```

### Select images with `filter()`

Every row is an image, and any selection of rows can be shown with
`tidymontage()`. Here four z-slices of one channel, with the slices as
columns. All slices share one display range, so the dimmer slices really have
less signal:

```{r zslices}
stack <- images |> filter(grepl("Airyscan", filepath))

stack |>
  filter(channel == "Alexa Fluor 488", z %in% c(1, 3, 5, 7)) |>
  tidymontage(x = z)
```

A single z-slice of all channels:

```{r filter-slice}
stack |>
  filter(z == 4) |>
  tidymontage()
```

### Project with `summarise()`

A maximum projection is a `summarise()` per channel. The result is still lazy:
`max of 7` is a recipe that is computed, plane by plane, only when the pixels
are needed.

```{r project}
projected <- stack |>
  summarise(img = max(img), .by = c(filepath, channel, color))
projected
```

```{r project-montage}
tidymontage(projected)
```

Projections can be restricted to part of the stack, just by filtering first:

```{r substack}
stack |>
  filter(z %in% 3:5) |>
  summarise(img = max(img), .by = channel)
```

`max()`, `min()` and `mean()` are available. Several projections side by side
are just several summaries, and `pivot_longer()` turns them back into rows:

```{r compare}
projections <- stack |>
  filter(channel == "Hoechst 33258") |>
  summarise(max = max(img), mean = mean(img), min = min(img), .by = c(filepath, channel, color)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(max, mean, min), names_to = "projection", values_to = "img")
projections
```

```{r compare-montage}
tidymontage(projections, x = projection)
```

All three projections are images of the same channel, so they share one
display range: the minimum projection really is that dim. To stretch each one
on its own, unlink them on purpose with
`adjust_exposure(.by = c(channel, projection))`.

### Describe the experiment with `mutate()` and joins

Conditions, targets or anything else are ordinary columns. The mutant came
from the file name above; the stained protein comes from a lookup table:

```{r describe}
targets <- tribble(
  ~channel,          ~target,
  "Cy3",             "HA-BCL-xL",
  "Alexa Fluor 488", "eGFP-L6",
  "DAPI",            "nuclei"
)

cells <- cells |>
  left_join(targets, by = "channel")

cells |> select(mutant, channel, target, color, img)
```

Columns like `target` can be used in the montage right away:

```{r describe-montage}
cells |>
  filter(target != "nuclei") |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, y = target)
```

The `color` column holds the default colour of each image, so changing it is
a `mutate()` as well. Nothing is re-read: colour is only used when images are
drawn. (Within a montage, `adjust_colors()` does the same.)

```{r recolor}
cells |>
  filter(mutant == "I56A") |>
  mutate(color = case_match(channel, "Cy3" ~ "#E69F00", "Alexa Fluor 488" ~ "#56B4E9", "DAPI" ~ "#FFFFFF")) |>
  tidymontage(x = target)
```

### Things that are refused

Images only support operations that make sense for images:

```{r refused, error = TRUE}
# summing intensities across images is not a projection
stack |> summarise(img = sum(img), .by = channel)

# images have no natural order
stack |> arrange(img)

# projecting images of different sizes (2024 x 2024 and 1796 x 1796 pixels)
images |> summarise(img = max(img), .by = channel_index)
```

## Build a montage

Like `tidyplot()` in tidyplots, `tidymontage()` takes the mapping: columns
mapped to `x` and `y` (here `mutant`) arrange blocks of panels, and the
**layout** arranges the channels and views within them. The default grid puts
the channels on the free axis:

```{r montage-grid}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant)
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(y = mutant)
```

From there on, `add_*()` and `adjust_*()` verbs decide everything about
display: merges, colours, display ranges, crops, zooms and scale bars.

### Merges

`add_merge()` adds a merge of channels as a virtual channel. It takes its
place in the layout like any other channel. Mapping `channel` (or a column
determined by it, such as `target`) yourself overrides where the layout puts
it:

```{r montage-merge}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = target, y = mutant) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI, name = "merge")
```

Channels are blended additively, each with its own colour and linked display
range. Member channels don't need panels of their own, and several merges are
possible:

```{r montage-merge-only}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = c(mutant, channel), channel = c("proteins", "all")) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, name = "proteins") |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI, name = "all")
```

Display ranges are **linked per channel** by default: both mutants share one
range per channel, so their brightness can be compared. `adjust_exposure()`
changes the percentiles or sets values, and `adjust_colors()` overrides the
colours from the metadata:

```{r montage-row}
montage <- projected |>
  tidymontage() |>
  adjust_colors(`Hoechst 33258` = "#56B4E9") |>
  adjust_exposure(min = "p0.1", max = "p99.8") |>
  add_merge(`Alexa Fluor 647`, `Alexa Fluor 555`, `Alexa Fluor 488`, `Hoechst 33258`)
montage
```

### Overlays: where channels coincide

`add_overlay()` adds a panel that is bright only where all of its channels
are bright, in a single colour. It is the minimum of the channels' display-
scaled intensities, so it is as bright as the weakest channel and isn't
stretched again: a faint overlap looks faint.

```{r overlay}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, channel = c("merge", "overlap")) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`) |>
  add_overlay(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, name = "overlap", color = "yellow") |>
  add_color_legend()
```

### Black channels: dark signal on white

A channel coloured black is shown inverted: dark signal on a white
background, with a thin frame. Merges always stay on black: there, black
channels use their original colour from the metadata, and `colors` in
`add_merge()` colours members differently in the merge only. Here both
proteins are black on their own, and the merge shows Cy3 in its original
magenta and Alexa Fluor 488 in yellow:

```{r ink}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, channel = c("Cy3", "Alexa Fluor 488", "merge")) |>
  adjust_colors(Cy3 = "black", `Alexa Fluor 488` = "black") |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, colors = c(`Alexa Fluor 488` = "yellow")) |>
  add_color_legend()
```

### Colormaps

Instead of a single colour, `lut()` colours a channel with a colormap such as
magma or viridis. Perceptually uniform maps show differences in intensity
more faithfully, which helps with quantitative images. Overlays can use a
colormap too. Merges need single colours, so there, colormap channels use
their original colour, like black channels do. The legend shows colormaps as
colour bars, labelled with the display range:

```{r colormaps}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, channel = c("Cy3", "overlap", "merge")) |>
  adjust_colors(Cy3 = lut("magma")) |>
  add_overlay(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, name = "overlap", color = lut("viridis")) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`) |>
  add_color_legend()
```

### Crops and zooms

`add_crop()` shows a region of each image. The size is given once, in
micrometres, so all panels share one magnification; only the position can
differ between images. Positions are the region's center, relative to the full
image (0-1), here one per mutant.

`add_zoom()` adds a blow-up as a new **view**: panels of their own, which the
grid places next to the main panels. A box marks the region on the main
panels, here only on the merges:

```{r crop-zoom}
crops <- tribble(
  ~mutant, ~x,   ~y,
  "I56A",  0.47, 0.40,
  "L59A",  0.42, 0.55
)
zooms <- tribble(
  ~mutant, ~x,   ~y,
  "I56A",  0.50, 0.40,
  "L59A",  0.40, 0.48
)

cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms, box = "merge")
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms, box = "merge") |> 
  preview_positions()
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms, box = "merge") |> 
  preview_exposure("DAPI")
```

Display ranges are computed from the full images, so cropping doesn't change
brightness. Map `view` yourself to put views elsewhere, and choose levels as
usual:

```{r zoom-rows}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, y = view, channel = "merge") |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_zoom(width = 20, center = zooms)
```

Rows and columns can differ in shape: all panels in a row share a height and
all panels in a column a width. So zooms can be flat strips, on rows of their
own below the crops:

```{r zoom-strips}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = channel, y = c(mutant, view)) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, height = 4, center = zooms)
```

Call `add_zoom()` again for more zooms. With two or more, each zoom gets a
number, shown in the top-left corner of its boxes and its panels, and the
views are named `"zoom 1"`, `"zoom 2"`, and so on:

```{r zoom-numbered}
zooms_2 <- tribble(
  ~mutant, ~x,   ~y,
  "I56A",  0.40, 0.55,
  "L59A",  0.52, 0.62
)

cells |>
  tidymontage(x = view, y = mutant, channel = "merge") |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms_2)
```

Crops and zooms can be rotated, for structures that run at an angle. The
angle is the one Fiji reports for a line drawn along the structure, in
degrees counterclockwise, and can differ between images. The panels show the
rotated regions upright. Zooms take the angle of the crop, so their boxes sit
square in it:

```{r rotated}
crops_rotated <- crops |>
  mutate(angle = c(30, -20))

cells |>
  tidymontage(x = view, y = mutant, channel = "merge") |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops_rotated) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms)
```

### Arrowheads

`add_arrows()` points at locations with arrowheads. An arrowhead belongs to an
image, not to a channel: it is drawn at the same place in every panel of that
image, merges included, and in zooms wherever its tip is inside. Positions are
given like the centers of crops, here several per mutant. Arrowheads are white
on dark panels and black on light ones:

```{r arrows}
arrows <- tribble(
  ~mutant, ~x,   ~y,
  "I56A",  0.45, 0.42,
  "I56A",  0.56, 0.40,
  "L59A",  0.41, 0.50
)

cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, channel = c("Cy3", "Alexa Fluor 488", "merge")) |>
  adjust_colors(`Alexa Fluor 488` = "black") |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`) |>
  add_arrows(arrows, size = 3)
```

### Finding exposure and positions

Two previews help to find the ballpark before fine-tuning the arguments.
`preview_exposure()` shows one image of a channel with 25 combinations of
display ranges, ordered by how the image looks: brighter to the right (lower
`max`), darker background downwards (higher `min`). The current setting is
outlined. The percentiles come from all images of the channel, as in the
montage:

```{r preview-exposure}
montage_cz <- cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms)

montage_cz |>
  preview_exposure("Cy3")
```

`preview_positions()` shows the full images with relative axes from 0 to 1,
the values that `center` in `add_crop()` and `add_zoom()` expects. The
current crop and zoom are outlined, which also shows their size:

```{r preview-positions}
montage_cz |>
  preview_positions()
```

### Hero layout

Layouts work like themes: the same montage with `layout = "hero"` shows one
big panel per block, by default the merge of the crop, next to the single
channels of the zoom, labelled outside the images. Nothing else changes:

```{r hero}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = "hero") |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |>
  add_scale_bar()
```

`layout_hero()` moves the small panels to the `"bottom"` or `"left"`,
`labels = FALSE` removes their labels, and `panel()` chooses other hero or
side panels:

```{r hero-bottom}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = layout_hero(position = "bottom", labels = FALSE)) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#F1CD36") |> 
  add_color_legend(position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = layout_hero(position = "bottom", side = panel(channel = c("Cy3", "Alexa Fluor 488", "merge"), view = c("zoom")))) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#F1CD36")
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = layout_hero(position = "bottom", side = panel(channel = c("Cy3", "Alexa Fluor 488", "merge"), view = c("zoom")))) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI, colors = c(DAPI = "#F1CD36")) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#000000", Cy3 = "#000000", `Alexa Fluor 488` = "#000000")
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = layout_hero(position = "bottom")) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI, colors = c(DAPI = "#F1CD36")) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#000000", Cy3 = "#000000", `Alexa Fluor 488` = "#000000")
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI, colors = c(DAPI = "#F1CD36")) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#000000", Cy3 = "#000000", `Alexa Fluor 488` = "#000000")

```

Side panels can have another shape than the hero. With `stack = TRUE`, they
are stacked: below the hero, each strip is as wide as the hero, for example
a flat zoom of each channel under a big merge:

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = layout_hero(position = "right", stack = TRUE)) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 4, height = 15, center = zooms) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_size(width = 160) |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#F1CD36") |> 
  add_color_legend(position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 4, height = 15, center = zooms) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_size(width = 160) |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#F1CD36") |> 
  add_color_legend(position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = layout_hero(position = "bottom", stack = TRUE)) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, height = 3, center = zooms) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_size(width = 160) |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#F1CD36") |> 
  add_color_legend(position = "bottom")
```

### Colour legend

`add_color_legend()` explains the colours, like a ggplot2 legend: a swatch
and the name of each channel shown, including the members of merges. In a
hero layout, it can replace the labels of the small panels.
It goes at the bottom (the default), on top or on the right, outside the panels, so the
montage grows and the panels keep their size:

```{r legend}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = layout_hero(position = "bottom", labels = FALSE)) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |>
  add_scale_bar() |>
  add_color_legend()
```

### Scale bars and headers

`add_scale_bar()` draws one scale bar per view, in its bottom-right panel; all
panels of a view share one magnification, so one bar is enough. Without a
length, a round length of about a fifth of the panel is chosen. Scale bars
need a known pixel size.

Row and column headers name the mapped levels. When several dimensions share
an axis, the headers are nested; `adjust_headers()` hides or restyles them:

```{r annotated}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms, box = "merge") |>
  add_scale_bar()
```

### Recipes and exact sizes

The montage keeps its recipe, and `get_panels()` shows the layout in mm
without reading any pixels:

```{r montage-recipe}
cat(format(montage), sep = "\n")
get_panels(montage)
```

Like plots in tidyplots, montages have a **fixed physical size**: by default,
the panels and gaps (without headers) fit into a box of 90 x 90 mm, keeping
the shape of the panels. Set the size in `tidymontage()` or later with
`adjust_size()`; `NA` leaves one side free. `tidymontage_options()` changes
the default for all montages of a session; this README uses
`tidymontage_options(width = 140, height = 140)`. Printing and saving use the
same size, so the figure looks the same on screen and in the file:

```{r save, eval = FALSE}
montage |>
  adjust_size(width = 180, height = NA) |>
  save_montage("figure.pdf")
#> Saved figure.pdf (180 x 40.2 mm).
```

### The layout explains itself

Every panel must show exactly one image, and the montage says so when it
doesn't:

```{r layout-errors, error = TRUE}
# two mutants, but only channels are mapped
cells |> tidymontage(x = channel) |> get_panels()

# levels can be chosen and ordered
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, channel = "DAPI") |>
  get_panels()

# unlinking display ranges across channels is possible, but flagged
tidymontage(cells, x = mutant) |> adjust_exposure(.by = mutant)
```
